name: CHAT (Centre for Heritage, Arts and Textile)
funding: Non-profit Mill6 Foundation, founded by Vanessa Cheung. Founding donor: D. H. Chen Foundation. Main donor: Nan Fung Group, the property group that owned the mills.
watch: Opened 16 March 2019 in a former Nan Fung cotton mill. ANTEPRIMA partners on the textile art prize.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; it names two donors, undated, and lists eight directors of Mill 6 Foundation, mostly Nan Fung Group executives.

name: Jehangir Art Gallery
watch: In April 2013 the gallery and Mumbai police made Eleena Banik remove two goddess paintings. In 2006 it had a student cover a nude sculpture.
why_flagged: Built 1952 on Sir Cowasji Jehangir's gift in memory of his son. A committee chaired by Adi H. Jehangir manages it; no sponsors or ongoing funders are listed.
records_note: The gallery names its management committee with chairman Adi Jehangir, but publishes no reports, accounts or sponsors.

name: Selasar Sunaryo Art Space
funding: Founded 1998 by artist Sunaryo with direction and support from the Selasar Sunaryo Foundation.
watch: Nonprofit art space in Bandung. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found. Earlier partner names (Goethe-Institut, Japan Foundation, British Council) are not on its site.
records_note: Its site posts no annual report, accounts, sponsor list or board; a 2010 ASEF profile names only the Selasar Sunaryo Foundation.

name: The Glucksman
funding: FY2025 income €871k: UCC subvention €428k, Arts Council €192k, other grants €13k, gifts €41k, plus shop, education and hire.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Sponsor pages unavailable. Gifts (€41k) and corporate sponsors are not named. Founding donor Lewis Glucksman was a Lehman banker; banks are allowed. No controversy found.
records_note: No annual report; posts 2025 audited financial statements and a 2025 board list, and names University College Cork and the Arts Council as funders.

name: Douglas Hyde Gallery
funding: FY2025 income €695k: Arts Council €378k, Trinity College Dublin €141k, sponsorship €19k, patrons €12k, plus €121k other income mostly from Ireland at Venice 2026 partners.
watch: Director's Circle includes Kerlin Gallery and mother's tankstation. The accounts do not name the Venice 2026 partners. No flagged funder or protest found.
records_note: No annual report; posts 2025 audited accounts, lists a ten-member board, and names its Arts Council and Trinity College support plus tiered patrons, undated.

name: Hugh Lane Gallery
watch: UNVERIFIED: Site blocks fetches. Live site returns 403. No accounts were read.
records_note: hughlane.ie blocked the check; parent Dublin City Council posts annual reports 2016 to 2025 and audited accounts 2015 to 2025.

name: Castello di Rivoli
funding: 2023 income €5.6M: public grants €3.2M (Regione Piemonte, Turin, Rivoli), private grants €1.3M (Fondazione CRT, CRC, Compagnia di San Paolo); Intesa Sanpaolo and Lavazza Group are partners.
watch: Francesca Lavazza chairs the board. Fondazione Magnetto funds a restoration. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: Rivoli posts yearly accounts and activity reports for 2017 to 2025 with auditors' reports, names its board, and names funders and sponsors in the accounts.

name: National Gallery of Jamaica
watch: CHASE Fund and the Tourism Enhancement Fund are public funds. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: The gallery's own site refused connections, and its parent, the Institute of Jamaica, posts no annual reports, accounts or board list on its site.

name: Aomori Museum of Art
watch: UNVERIFIED: Exhibition sponsor list not readable. Current schedule pages (e.g. No controversy found in a Japanese-language search.
records_note: The museum posts yearly reports from 2006 to 2023 with budget and outturn tables, and an undated list of corporate supporters, but no board list.

name: Hakone Open-Air Museum
funding: The foundation says it runs mainly on admission income. Founded 1968 by the Fujisankei Group (Fuji Television, Sankei Shimbun, Nippon Broadcasting); 173 firms paid for construction. Donations accepted.
watch: No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: The foundation posts statutes and a dated board list but no annual report, accounts or donor list; it says admissions fund most of its work.

name: Pola Museum of Art
funding: Pola Art Foundation, set up in May 1996 with the personal assets of Tsuneji Suzuki of the Pola founding family; a public-interest foundation since July 2010.
watch: No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: The Pola Art Foundation posts business reports for FY2021 to FY2025, balance sheets and net-asset statements, and a board list; it names no donors.

name: Ohara Museum of Art
funding: Ohara Art Foundation. Official partners (1 April 2026) include Kurabo, Kuraray, Chugoku Bank, Sanyo Shimbun, ENEOS Mizushima refinery, Okayama Gas, Yokoyama Sekiyu and Japan Tobacco, plus over 200 other firms.
watch: ENEOS Mizushima refinery, Okayama Gas and Yokoyama Sekiyu are fossil fuel partners; Japan Tobacco is a tobacco partner. All are on the 2026 list.
why_flagged: Ohara Art Foundation. Official partners (1 April 2026) include Kurabo, Kuraray, Chugoku Bank, Sanyo Shimbun, ENEOS Mizushima refinery, Okayama Gas, Yokoyama Sekiyu and Japan Tobacco, plus over 200 other firms.
records_note: Its foundation posts yearly business reports for 2024 and 2025, financial statements and a director list; partners are logos dated April 2026.
